page: UpCloud PREMIUM-64xCPU-128GB is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory, which yields a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU allocation is designated as shared. Storage is bundled as a 500 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in both single-core and multi-core computational tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place this instance in the top 10% of tested hardware, a tier also matched by its PassMark CPU score of 89,600.48 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 574.99 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient at 8,284.04 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to 259.03 GB/sec and 124.18 GB/sec respectively. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in LLM inference, where prompt processing for a small 135M model registers at 69.99 tokens/sec, falling into the bottom 10% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high compute density with its 64 physical cores, making it a viable option for highly parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory-to-core ratios. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong database operations benchmark of 30,685.25 operations per second indicate suitability for multi-threaded processing, database hosting, and high-throughput static web serving. However, the shared CPU allocation model may introduce performance variability under sustained peak loads compared to dedicated resource environments.
